business_problem: Banco do Brasil needed a trustworthy way to scale AI across critical banking functions while satisfying regulatory, ethical and public-accountability obligations around transparency, control, explainability and risk management.
solution_summary: Banco do Brasil worked with EY and IBM to operationalize a unified AI-governance model built for a heavily regulated public financial institution. EY designed the governance frameworks for generative AI lifecycle management and continuous AI monitoring, while IBM implemented the operating layer with IBM watsonx.governance. The platform automates supervision across the AI journey, from model design and evaluation through deployment into critical banking environments, and adds real-time monitoring, customized metrics, proactive alerts, traceability and version control for AI assets. Banco do Brasil is testing the combined framework in generative AI use cases so performance, compliance and risk requirements can be checked continuously rather than through sporadic manual review. This gives the bank a technical control plane for responsible AI adoption, turning governance from policy documents into a repeatable operating system for analytics and model oversight.

solution_components.name: IBM watsonx.governance
solution_components.role: Automates AI oversight with monitoring, explainability, alerts and traceability across Banco do Brasil's model lifecycle.

data_flow: AI models and assets move through EY-defined lifecycle and monitoring frameworks, while watsonx.governance captures evaluations, metrics, alerts, explainability and version history so compliance and risk teams can supervise models continuously from design through deployment.
business_outcome: Banco do Brasil improved oversight, agility and institutional trust in AI, giving the bank a scalable way to validate that models meet ethics, security and performance standards before and after deployment.
architecture_clues: The bank defines roles and responsibilities from model design through production deployment.
The framework includes benchmarking and vulnerability assessment for foundational models.
The operating model is being tested first in generative AI use cases.
